previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A woman with type 1 diabetes was admitted for diabetic ketoacidosis triggered by emotional stress and missed insulin. She presented with severe nausea, vomiting, and anxiety after a family conflict. Treatment included an insulin drip and IV fluids, with resolution of DKA. Her nausea improved slowly, and she resumed oral intake. The Lantus dose was reduced to 25 units at discharge to prevent hypoglycemia. She was counseled to avoid non-prescribed narcotics, which could worsen gastroparesis and glycemic control. Social work and mental health support were recommended due to recurrent admissions linked to stress and depression. She was discharged home in stable condition with follow-up plans.

Brief Hospital Course:
ASSESSMENT & PLAN:  ___ with DM1 and recurrent episodes of

#  Severe viral gastritis:  Patient was admitted with severe 
nausea/vomiting and epigastric cramping pain to the point that 
she was unable to take POs.  Given the acuity of these symptoms 
and her initial leukocytosis and low grade fevers, she was felt 
to have a viral gastritis.  CTA unremarkable with no evidence of 
ischemic colitis and demonstrated patent vasculature.  Due to 
the prolonged course, Gastroenterology was consulted and EGD was 
performed that only showed mild esophagitis and an area of 
patchy erythema.  Biopsy results for H. pylori are pending at 
discharge.  

During her hospitalization, she was given a trial of Reglan that 
did not help.  However, she is noted to have several 
hospitalizations for N/V and may benefit from an outpatient 
gastric emptying stomach.  Prior to hospitalization, she had 
taken narcotics for her chronic back pain, so the study was not 
performed as an inpatient.  An outpatient GI appointment was 
made for her.  She was advised to stay away from narcotics.  
.  
# Diabetic ketoacidosis, DM1:  Patient on admission had a blood 
glucose of 233, an anion gab of 18, and bicarb of 16.  This 
quickly improved with IVFs and insulin.  Trigger for DKA may be 
viral gastroenteritis or bronchiolitis.  She then had issues 
with hypoglycemia with her decreased ability to take pos.  Her 
Lantus dose is currently down to 16 units and needs to be 
titrated. 
.  
# Bronchiolitis: Pt does endorse cough, sob and tree and ___ 
opacities were seen on CT. CXR, however, was insignificant.  
Given the her DKA and the degree of her nasuea/vomiting, she was 
treated with a 5 day course of levofloxacin.
.  
# Panic attacks:  Patient had several panic attacks while 
hospitalized, lasting a few minutes.  She was started on 
citalopram 10 mg daily, titrated up to 20 mg upon discharge.  
She will follow up with her PCP.

Discharge Instructions:
You were admitted for nausea and vomiting.  This is suspected to 
be from a virus.  You also had an upper endoscopy to look in 
your stomach.  You were found to have a mild irritation of the 
esophagus and patchy redness in your stomach, most likely from 
repeated vomiting.  You were able to eat food without vomiting 
by discharge.

You were also found to have diabetic ketoacidosis on admission.  
Please adhere to your insulin regimen.

You were also found to have a pneumonia.  You have completed 
your course of antibiotic levofloxacin for this.

Please see the attached medication list:
--Please continue to take your pantoprazole (Protonix) to 40 mg 
once a day.
--We have also decreased your Lantus to 20 units.  Please check 
your fingersticks before meals and before bedtime.  If your 
morning fasting sugar is >120 for three days in a row, please 
increase your Lantus by ___ units every 3 days until your 
morning fasting sugar is consistently <120.
--You were also started on citalopram (Celexa) for anxiety.  You 
MUST follow up with your primary care provider to continue this.
--We tried tramadol for your back pain.  If this helped, please 
call your primary care provider for future management.  There is 
a low risk that tramadol may interact with citalopram.  Please 
do not take pain medications prescribed to other people.

If you develop worsening nausea/vomiting/abdominal pain, fevers, 
or any other concerning symptoms, please call your primary care 
provider.

radiology_notes.text:
INDICATION:  ___ female with nausea and vomiting.  Assess for stones
or cholecystitis.

COMPARISON:  Abdominal CT ___.

FINDINGS:  The liver shows no focal or textural abnormality.  There is no
biliary dilatation and the common duct measures 0.2 cm.  The portal vein is
patent with hepatopetal flow.  The gallbladder is normal without evidence of
stones.  There is no gallbladder wall edema and no pericholecystic fluid is
identified.  The pancreas is unremarkable.

Incidentally noted on limited images, the right kidney appears to be somewhat
echogenic.

IMPRESSION:

1.  Normal right upper quadrant with no gallstones and no signs of
cholecystitis.
2.  Mildly echogenic right kidney seen on limited images.  This is an
equivocal finding as it may simply represent a lack of intraabdominal fat.
Clinical correlation with renal function tests is suggested.
